model: Airless apparent angles of the Sun and Earth centers (libration included by Horizons); visible = center elevation > threshold above a reference horizon with no terrain; linear interpolation between samples; no power, antenna or link model.
terrain_model: Sites with a 'terrain' block also carry windows computed against the real horizon from LOLA topography: visible = center elevation > horizon(azimuth). Sites without it only have the reference-horizon model; missing terrain data does not mean a clear horizon.
time_convention: All times are Unix seconds in UTC

sites.name: Shackleton-de Gerlache Connecting Ridge (C1)
sites.context: One of the most illuminated spots near the lunar south pole. 'Connecting Ridge' was one of the 13 candidate regions NASA announced in August 2022 for the first crewed landing (then planned as Artemis III), but it is not in NASA's updated list of nine (October 2024). NASA now plans that first landing as Artemis IV, in 2028.
sites.source: Glaser et al. (2018), Illumination conditions at the lunar poles: Implications for future exploration, Planetary and Space Science 162, Table (Connecting Ridge C1: -89.4398, 222.83 E)

terrain.model: Terrain horizon from LOLA elevation models: exact 3D geometry on a 1737.4 km sphere (curvature included), point observer, highest terrain elevation angle per azimuth bin. No atmosphere. DEM interpolation between LOLA tracks is a known limitation.
sources: NASA/GSFC PGDA product 78, LOLA 5 m/pix Site01 Connecting Ridge (Barker et al. 2021), https://pgda.gsfc.nasa.gov/products/78

sites.name: IM-2 Athena landing site, Mons Mouton (CLPS)
sites.context: NASA CLPS delivery by Intuitive Machines, landed 6 March 2025. LROC notes the intended site lies in the central portion of a potential landing region for the first crewed landing; Mons Mouton is one of the nine candidate regions NASA selected in October 2024 for that landing, then planned as Artemis III. NASA now plans it as Artemis IV, in 2028.
sites.source: LROC (NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University), 'IM-2 Athena Seen Obliquely'

terrain.model: Terrain horizon from LOLA elevation models: exact 3D geometry on a 1737.4 km sphere (curvature included), point observer, highest terrain elevation angle per azimuth bin. No atmosphere. DEM interpolation between LOLA tracks is a known limitation.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram landing site (ISRO, India)
sites.context: India's lander, 23 August 2023, about 600 km from the south pole.

sites.name: Chang'e-4 landing site, Von Karman crater (CNSA, China, far side)
sites.context: First landing on the lunar far side, 3 January 2019. Earth is never above the horizon here; communication goes through a relay satellite.
sites.source: LROC (NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University), 'Chang'e 4 Lander Coordinates' (+/- 20 m)

sites.name: Apollo 11, Tranquility Base
sites.context: Equatorial near-side site, 20 July 1969: about 14 days of light and 14 of night, Earth almost fixed in the sky.
sites.source: NASA NSSDC, Apollo Landing Site Coordinates (Lunar Module)
